slug: 2025-08-12 Zambia sees civil registration as bedrock of inclusive digital transformation
note: States modernisation and digitisation as a government aim and a 50 percent birth registration target, but names no digital register procured, piloted or in service.

slug: 2025-06-12 Zambia says using multiple strategies to meet 50 percent birth registration goal by 2026
note: Birth registration is 14 percent (UNICEF, 2024), below 90 percent; digitisation is described as intent with no digital civil register named.

facts.fact: The Lavushimanda district registration officer said digital civil registration, covering birth registration, runs on INRIS, which was deployed to 26 district national registration offices in March 2022 (Lusaka Times, 3 September 2026).
The same official said the exercise run on INRIS covers securing death certificates as well as birth registration (Lusaka Times, 3 September 2026).

note: Registration rates stated are 22 percent of under-fives and 28 percent of deaths, below 90 percent; no digital civil register is named.

systems.system: Sample Based Registration System with Vital Statistics (SRS-VS)

note: SRS-VS is a sample-based mortality surveillance system, not a digital civil register.

facts.fact: INRIS, the civil registration and legal identity information management system, has been rolled out in 79 districts, covering all city and municipal councils, with some district councils pending, per the INRIS deputy project manager.

systems.owner: Department of National Registration, Passports and Citizenship

facts.fact: The 2017 vital statistics report says birth notifications validated by district registrars are entered in the electronic civil register, with registered births of 104,816 in 2017 counted from the electronic database, and that births of 2013 and 2014 were largely on paper and not entered; health-facility notification was only starting in selected facilities.
The 2017 vital statistics report says birth and death notifications are entered in the district register and then in the electronic civil register, from which 2017 death statistics were produced.
